page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs consisting of 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The CPU includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, which accelerate vector and neural network operations. This instance operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates consistent mid-tier performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yields a score of 30666.35, while the single-core performance reaches 1436.68. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for cached operations, registering 1705.41 GB/sec for small blocks, though it drops to 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations, measured via PassMark, score 11442.59, and Redis SET operations achieve 28.91 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning, the instance processes 135M parameter LLM prompts at 1539.55 tokens per second, though performance drops to 45.98 tokens per second for a 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage over its 10 Gbps baseline network interface. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high clock speed provide predictable compute performance without the premium of GPU-accelerated hardware. This profile is appropriate for workloads such as relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks.
